rows.description: A young person, especially from a poor, minority or lower-caste background, feels talked down to or threatened. Recording facts, involving family, lawyers or human-rights groups, and staying calm are safer than resisting physically.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: shyness, calm, trust

rows.description: A driver at a checkpoint faces a fine and a hint of settling on the spot. Paying the official fine with a receipt is lawful; offering money privately is a bribe and risks more trouble.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Respect for law while seeking change [Response]
rows.description: A young adult who thinks a law is unjust chooses petitions, votes and courts rather than breaking it quietly or violently. Working through lawful means keeps protection intact while pressing for reform.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A child is told to stand in line for a slide or the school water tap and pushes when impatient. Taking turns is one of the first civic lessons, and small children learn it with praise and clear examples.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child throws a wrapper on the road because grown-ups do. Children copy what they see; a parent who pockets the trash teaches more than any lecture.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager rides a scooter without a helmet or overtakes recklessly to look daring. Belief in one's own safety is strong at this age, and peer pressure feeds it; respected adults and real stories can shift habits.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult slips ahead in a ticket line because it is quicker and others do it too. The small gain costs trust, and calmly asking someone to join the back of the line often works.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A driver hit by a small scrape shouts and threatens, feeling disrespected and rushed. Anger in traffic is adrenaline and pride; breathing, leaving the scene and letting insurance handle it prevents worse.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: admiration, anger, pride, relief from stress

rows.description: A young commuter offers a seat to an elder, a pregnant woman or a disabled person without waiting to be asked. Public kindness is contagious, and others soon copy it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A bystander asks a man spitting or harassing others to stop, calmly and with a friend nearby. Safety comes first; speaking in a neutral tone and calling authorities when needed keeps things from escalating.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
